brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.requirement: A planter (a container for growing plants)
requirements.evidence: Three hex base pieces at cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) each holding a bin with soil: bin drain at (-1,0) and (1,0), 3-compartment bin at (0,0). Joined with two joint bolts; check_build reports meshClash clear and no errors.
basil-young in the bin at (-1,0,0), thyme-young in the bin at (0,0,0), rosemary-young in the bin at (1,0,0); check_build shows no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or prop warnings.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for a sunny kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Footprint is about 478 x 89 x 335 mm, a low row of three cells, and the herbs chosen (basil, thyme, rosemary) are sun-tolerant Mediterranean types. The configurator cannot verify sun exposure, heat or UV resistance of the printed material, so that part is unverified.

Two cells use drained bins (hex-bin-full-drain). The middle cell uses a 3-compartment bin without drain holes, so that one is not drained; I did not change it. Drainage holes are geometry only; the configurator does not check watertightness.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell planter row on a sunny sill footprint: three hex bases with bins, each filled with soil and planted with one herb (basil, thyme, rosemary), joined by two joint bolts. Mesh check is clear. Limitations: the middle bin lacks drain holes, and the material's suitability for sun, heat and water is not something the configurator can verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
